short: General Data Key/Value Store and Execution
introduction: ERC-725 defines two building blocks for smart contract accounts: a key/value data store (ERC725Y) mapping bytes32 keys to arbitrary bytes values, and a generic execution function (ERC725X) for calling, creating, or delegatecalling other contracts. It was proposed by Fabian Vogelsteller and Tyler Yasaka in October 2017. Both parts are owner-controlled via ERC-173 and usable together or separately. Note: ERC-725 is a Draft; the specification is still under active development and may change substantially.
designPurpose: ERC-725 was designed to give smart contract accounts a data and execution layout flexible enough to last long-term yet standardized enough for tooling to rely on. Before it, each project invented its own storage variables and execution entry points, so external contracts and off-chain apps could not read or drive them uniformly. Keeping all data under one mapping(bytes32 => bytes) and routing outgoing actions through a single execute function lets protocols reinterpret its data without changing the interface.
commonUsage: ERC-725 serves as a foundation for modular smart contract accounts and for upgradable on-chain metadata. Its ERC725Y store is used on its own to attach mutable metadata to NFTs, tokens, and other contracts, while ERC725X provides a generic execute entry point for account-style contracts that act on a user's behalf. The spec notes that the account form is standardized as LSP0-ERC725Account, with LSP2-ERC725JSONSchema defining how keys and values are encoded.
fn.execute.desc: Executes a single operation from the account: a call, contract creation with CREATE or CREATE2, staticcall, or delegatecall, selected by operationType. May only be called by the current owner and reverts if the operation fails.
fn.execute.params.operationType: The operation type to perform: 0 for CALL, 1 for CREATE, 2 for CREATE2, 3 for STATICCALL, or 4 for DELEGATECALL.
fn.execute.params.target: The contract or address to call; should be address(0) when creating a contract.
fn.execute.params.value: The amount of native token to transfer, in wei.
fn.execute.params.data: The call data, or the creation bytecode when deploying a contract.
fn.execute.returns.returnData: The data returned by the called function, or the address of the deployed contract.
fn.executeBatch.desc: Executes a batch of operations in one transaction, taking equal-length arrays of operation types, targets, values, and call data. Only the owner may call it, and it reverts if any operation fails.
fn.executeBatch.params.operationsType: The list of operation types to perform for each call.
fn.executeBatch.params.targets: The list of addresses to call for each operation.
fn.executeBatch.params.values: The list of native token amounts to transfer, in wei.
fn.executeBatch.params.datas: The list of call data or contract creation bytecode.
fn.executeBatch.returns.results: The array of returned data or deployed contract addresses.
fn.getData.desc: Returns the bytes value stored under a single data key in the ERC725Y store. Any caller can read it.
fn.getData.params.dataKey: The data key whose value to retrieve.
fn.getData.returns.dataValue: The bytes value stored for the requested data key.
fn.getDataBatch.desc: Returns the values stored under multiple data keys in one call, keeping gas costs low for bulk reads.
fn.getDataBatch.params.dataKeys: The list of data keys whose values to retrieve.
fn.getDataBatch.returns.dataValues: The array of bytes values for the requested data keys.
fn.setData.desc: Stores a bytes value under a single data key in the ERC725Y store, overwriting any previous value. Only the owner may call it, and it emits DataChanged.
fn.setData.params.dataKey: The data key whose value to set.
fn.setDataBatch.desc: Stores values under multiple data keys in one call, taking equal-length arrays of keys and values. Only the owner may call it, and it emits DataChanged for each key.
fn.setDataBatch.params.dataKeys: The list of data keys whose values to set.
fn.setDataBatch.params.dataValues: The list of bytes values to store.
fn.Executed.desc: Emitted when execute performs a CALL, STATICCALL, or DELEGATECALL (operation types 0, 3, and 4).
fn.Executed.params.operationType: The operation type that was executed.
fn.Executed.params.value: The amount of native token sent, in wei.
fn.Executed.params.data: The first four bytes of the call data, typically the function selector.
fn.ContractCreated.desc: Emitted when execute deploys a new contract via CREATE or CREATE2 (operation types 1 and 2).
fn.ContractCreated.params.operationType: The operation type used to deploy the contract.
fn.ContractCreated.params.contractAddres: The address of the newly deployed contract.
fn.ContractCreated.params.value: The amount of native token sent to the new contract, in wei.
fn.ContractCreated.params.salt: The bytes32 salt used for a CREATE2 deployment.
fn.DataChanged.desc: Emitted whenever a data key's value is successfully set in the ERC725Y store.
fn.DataChanged.params.dataKey: The data key whose value changed.
fn.DataChanged.params.dataValue: The new bytes value stored for the key.
sim.setDataWalkthrough.name: Set Data Walkthrough
sim.setDataWalkthrough.desc: Follow a setData call from the owner through the ERC725Y data store to the DataChanged event.
sim.setDataWalkthrough.step.call: The owner calls setData(dataKey, dataValue) on the ERC-725 account to store a value.
sim.setDataWalkthrough.step.execute: The contract checks that the caller is the owner, then writes the value into the bytes32-to-bytes data store, overwriting any previous value for the key.
sim.setDataWalkthrough.step.event: The contract emits DataChanged(dataKey, dataValue) so indexers and off-chain apps can track the update.
